metadata.summary: CheXpert is a large chest radiograph dataset containing 224,316 chest radiographs of 65,240 patients. It includes automatically extracted labels for 14 observations from radiology reports, with explicit uncertainty annotations to reflect interpretive ambiguity.

papers.title: CheXpert — A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison

metadata.purpose: To serve as a standard benchmark for training and evaluating deep learning models on chest radiograph interpretation, particularly addressing uncertainty in radiological reporting.

ethics.privacy_measures: De-identification performed per HIPAA Safe Harbor standards; all 18 identifiers removed; radiographs anonymized.
ethics.legal_compliance: Compliant with HIPAA and Stanford IRB Protocol #35576.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.

known_limitations: Single-center origin limits generalizability to other institutions, populations, or imaging protocols.
Labels derived from radiology reports—not ground truth pathology—introduce reporting bias and linguistic ambiguity.
No demographic metadata released; inability to assess or mitigate performance disparities across sex, race, or age groups.
Frontal and lateral views only; absence of other projections or modalities (e.g., CT).
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Yes: labels are algorithmically derived and recoded into uncertainty-aware categories (Positive/Negative/Uncertain/Blank); original reports are not released.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: 90%+ from a single US academic medical center; unknown geographic, ethnic, socioeconomic, and temporal representativeness.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Yes: several observations (e.g., 'Enlarged Cardiomediastinum', 'Pleural Other') exhibit low prevalence and high label uncertainty.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Performance may degrade on images from different manufacturers, protocols, or patient populations due to domain shift; temporal drift (2002–2017) uncharacterized.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic attributes (age, sex, race) are not included in the public release.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Not intended for detection or segmentation; no pixel-level annotations provided.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Patients were selected from the electronic health record (EHR) system at Stanford Hospital; inclusion was based on availability of chest radiographs and associated radiology reports.
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Consecutive radiographic studies from Stanford Hospital EHR between 2002 and 2017; no explicit stratification or random sampling described in source text.
data_origin.data_shifts_overtime: Data collected from 2002–2017; potential temporal shifts in imaging equipment, reporting practices, and clinical protocols not quantified in source text.

population.target_population: Adult patients undergoing chest radiography at Stanford Hospital.
population.inclusion_criteria: Presence of chest radiograph and corresponding radiology report in Stanford Hospital EHR.
population.missing_groups: No demographic subgroup statistics reported; underrepresentation of non-White, non-US, pediatric, and elderly subgroups cannot be ruled out.

annotation.annotation_method: Labels for 14 observations automatically extracted from radiology reports using rule-based NLP; uncertainty labels (Uncertain, Positive, Negative, Blank) assigned per observation based on report phrasing.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Derived from free-text radiology reports via NLP labeler; validated against expert annotations on subsets.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label noise arises from ambiguity in natural language reports (e.g., 'no evidence of pneumonia' vs. 'pneumonia cannot be excluded'); uncertainty labels explicitly encode this.
